result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A says outright that the spec is sound and names the decisions worth keeping; B goes straight to listing problems. Both make the same main fixes (multi-page conflict, missing states, merchant source, unready drafts on submit), and both reprint the whole spec. A adds extras like on-phone reading and a screen-reader note, and its multi-page Done button adds a small step. B keeps the no-save-step rule more cleanly but makes more minor edits (30 days, singular button text). | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same real problems: item 1 conflicts with item 7, item 3 leaves out states, merchant isn't read from the photo, and item 6 doesn't say what happens to unready drafts. Both also reprint the whole spec, which hurts them on brevity. A's fixes stay smaller and keep the no-save-step rule for multi-page by having later photos join the first draft. B adds a Done button, which brings back a save step, and also adds things nobody asked for: on-device reading, a screen-reader announcement and a link to fix drafts. B does say up front that the spec is sound, and A does not.
